Experiment_description: The experiments conducted in this stage explored the implementation of machine learning models, specifically logistic regression and feedforward neural networks, on synthetic datasets to predict the Reviewer Quality Index (RQI) within a bi-directional feedback and rewards framework for peer review quality assessment.
Significance: These experiments are significant as they test the initial feasibility of using machine learning models to predict reviewer quality from synthetic data. The findings indicate effective learning and generalization capabilities of simple models, providing a foundation for further exploration and refinement of models and data preprocessing techniques. Successful implementation could lead to improved peer review systems, enhancing the reliability and accountability of the review process.
Description: The nodes implemented logistic regression and feedforward neural networks to predict RQI based on synthetic datasets simulating peer review processes. The experiments tracked metrics such as training and validation loss and RQI to evaluate model performance. These initial implementations aimed to establish baseline methods and analyze their effectiveness in predicting reviewer quality, with a focus on model convergence, generalization, and stability.
